title: Document: mobile_compliance.txt
text:
Document [mobile_compliance.txt]: 1. OVERVIEW
Project Mobile App Revamp (PRJ-003) is currently in the DESIGN phase. It mandates FaceID and TouchID biometric authentication for high-value financial transactions.

title: Document: mobile_compliance.txt
text:
Document [mobile_compliance.txt]: 2. COMPLIANCE & SECURITY REQUIREMENTS
- iOS SDK 18.2 LocalAuthentication framework required.
- Android KeyStore hardware-backed biometric prompt required.
- Risk Flag: Beta iOS SDK changes may cause biometric fallback failures on older device models.
- Mitigation Action: Maintain fallback PIN/OTP secondary authentication flow for non-biometric devices.

title: Document: orion_sow.txt
text:
Document [orion_sow.txt]: 1. PROJECT SUMMARY
Project Orion Upgrade focuses on modernizing core enterprise legacy backend services into cloud-native microservices, optimizing database performance, and migrating on-premise workloads to multi-region cloud infrastructure.

title: Document: orion_sow.txt
text:
Document [orion_sow.txt]: 2. LIFECYCLE PHASE: MOBILIZATION
- Duration: May 1, 2025 to August 28, 2025
- Key Milestones:
  * M1.1: Vendor Contract Finalization & SLA Sign-off (Target: May 10, 2025)
  * M1.2: Resource Onboarding & Security Access Provisioning (Target: May 20, 2025)
  * M1.3: Third-Party API Integration Specification Review (Target: May 25, 2025)
  * M1.4: Legacy Database Refactoring & Schema Validation (Target: June 15, 2025)

title: Document: orion_sow.txt
text:
Document [orion_sow.txt]: 3. KNOWN RISKS AND ASSUMPTIONS
- Risk R-001 (Vendor API Delay): Dependency on CloudCorp API v3.2 release. If delayed beyond May 20, mock server endpoints must be deployed.
- Assumption A-001: Legacy Oracle DB tables are assumed to contain valid UTF-8 strings without orphan foreign key constraints.
- Dependency D-001: Final deployment requires operational handover sign-off from Enterprise SecOps.

title: Document: orion_sow.txt
text:
Document [orion_sow.txt]: 4. DELIVERABLES & ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA
- 99.95% system uptime on cloud microservices.
- Zero unmasked PII in application logs.
- Executive status reports generated weekly for PMO review.

title: Document: pegasus_architecture.txt
text:
Document [pegasus_architecture.txt]: 1. OVERVIEW
Project Pegasus (PRJ-002) is currently in the PLANNING phase. It involves integrating the enterprise ERP system with modern microservices via asynchronous event-driven queues (RabbitMQ/Kafka).

title: Document: pegasus_architecture.txt
text:
Document [pegasus_architecture.txt]: 2. ARCHITECTURAL DEPENDENCIES & ASSUMPTIONS
- Database Schema: PostgreSQL 16 master database with read-replicas. Legacy migration from Oracle 11g.
- Risk Flag: High probability of schema mismatch during automated script migration due to legacy column data types (RAW vs BYTEA).
- Mitigation Strategy: Perform staging ETL dry-runs with 100% field validation scripts before production cutover.

title: Document: risk_sop.txt
text:
Document [risk_sop.txt]: 1. RAID CATEGORIES DEFINITION
All program risk analysis and stakeholder communications must categorize project items into four RAID pillars:
- Risk (R): Potential future events that may negatively impact project objectives (e.g. vendor delay, budget variance).
- Assumption (A): Factors considered true for planning purposes without concrete proof (e.g. legacy data cleanliness).
- Issue (I): Current active problems impacting cost, schedule, or quality (e.g. IT access bottleneck).
- Dependency (Dep): External or internal task completions required before a project task can proceed (e.g. SecOps clearance).

title: Document: risk_sop.txt
text:
Document [risk_sop.txt]: 2. RISK SCORING METHODOLOGY
Risk Score = Likelihood (1-10) x Impact (1-10)
- High Risk (Score 70 - 100): Triggers mandatory Executive Alert email and instant mitigation plan generation.
- Medium Risk (Score 40 - 69): Managed by Project Manager with bi-weekly PMO status updates.
- Low Risk (Score 1 - 39): Monitored by Team Lead during sprint planning.

title: Document: risk_sop.txt
text:
Document [risk_sop.txt]: 3. STAKEHOLDER COMMUNICATION TONE & WORDING RULES
- Executive Stakeholders: Concise executive summary focusing on financial impact, delayed milestones, and strategic mitigation options.
- Technical Leads & Developers: Detailed technical root cause, API endpoint specifics, stack trace logs, and code workarounds.
- Project Managers: Timeline adjustments, resource reallocation needs, dependency maps, and WBS impact.
- External Clients: Professional, polished summary emphasizing resolution action plans, customer protection, and updated delivery dates.

title: Document: risk_sop.txt
text:
Document [risk_sop.txt]: 4. HUMAN APPROVAL MANDATE FOR AI GENERATED EMAILS
No AI-generated stakeholder email or report may be dispatched directly to external or executive recipients without explicit Human Approval (Status update: PENDING -> APPROVED) in the Communication Center.

title: Document: security_policy.txt
text:
Document [security_policy.txt]: 1. OVERVIEW AND OBJECTIVE
This policy governs data privacy, Personally Identifiable Information (PII) handling, and security compliance across all enterprise IT programs, software delivery initiatives, and third-party integrations. All project managers, technical leads, software developers, and external vendors must strictly adhere to these protocols.

title: Document: security_policy.txt
text:
Document [security_policy.txt]: 2. PII CLASSIFICATION AND MASKING MANDATE
- Level 1 (Restricted PII): Social Security Numbers (SSN), credit card numbers, biometric templates, and personal passwords. Level 1 PII MUST NEVER be stored in plain text, logged in application trace files, or passed to external LLMs/APIs.
- Level 2 (Confidential PII): Full employee/client names, personal email addresses, phone numbers, and financial salary bands. Level 2 PII must be masked or anonymized (e.g., regex/NER redaction) prior to sending data to AI agents or RAG vector indexes.
- Level 3 (Internal Business Data): Project codes, task titles, non-confidential status reports, and technical architectural diagrams.

title: Document: security_policy.txt
text:
Document [security_policy.txt]: 3. THIRD-PARTY API INTEGRATION & VENDOR SECURITY RULES
- Vendors providing third-party APIs must undergo mandatory SecOps audit clearance every 6 months.
- Any third-party API integration delay exceeding 5 business days triggers an automatic Risk Level High escalation to the Program Management Office (PMO).
- Fallback mock servers or synthetic test stubs must be utilized during vendor outage windows to avoid blocking critical path sprint timelines.

title: Document: security_policy.txt
text:
Document [security_policy.txt]: 4. DATA RETENTION AND AUDIT LOGGING
- Audit logs capturing user access, administrative overrides, AI prompt executions, and role permissions must be retained in an immutable database store for a minimum of 36 months.
- System administrators are audited quarterly for privileged role updates.
